source.title: Seminar Notes on Open Questions in Iwasawa Theory - SNOQIT I: The Λ[G]-modules of Iwasawa theory II: Units and Kummer theory in Iwasawa extensions

accepted.question_text: Beyond the class-group modules that arise in classical Iwasawa theory, which other Λ-modules have Property F, and what general hypotheses guarantee that a submodule of a free Λ-module has Property F? The question asks for intrinsic structural criteria, not just isolated examples, so that one can recognize when a projective-limit Λ-module has the same rigidity and decomposition behavior that the paper proves for the standard Iwasawa modules.

evidence.quote: While the property itself can be retained in a simple axiom, it is an important open question, to find out other examples of modules with property F, and possibly some general conditions under which a submodule of a free Λ-module has this property.

accepted.question_text: For the Iwasawa module A′ built from the p-parts of the ideal class groups of the p-integers in the cyclotomic tower of a Galois number field K, is the T-torsion subgroup A′[T] always finite? Equivalently, does the generalized Gross-Kuz'min conjecture hold outside the special cases proved here, so that the T-primary obstruction in the p-unit class-group module is never infinite?

evidence.quote: We consider here however the generalized Conjecture of Kuz’min and Gross, which states that A′[T] is finite.
Theorem 1. Let K be a CM extension of Q. Then Leopoldt’s conjecture holds for K and A′[T] is finite.

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary number field K and a fixed prime p, does the Leopoldt defect D(K) vanish? In concrete terms, is the p-adic closure of the global unit group always as large as Leopoldt predicted, so that no unexpected p-adic rank defect occurs in the unit embedding?

evidence.quote: The global units En embed diagonally in Un and their completion in the product topology is written En ⊂ Un. There may be a rank loss in this completion step and the possible difference D(Kn) := Z-rk(En) − Zp-rk(En) is called the Leopoldt defect, since Leopoldt conjected in 1962 the vanishing of D(Kn), at least for abelian extensions of Q. After the proof of this fact in 1967, by Baker and Brumer, the fact that D(K) = 0 for all number fields remained as an open conjecture, which also caries the name of Leopoldt.
Theorem 1. Let K be a CM extension of Q. Then Leopoldt’s conjecture holds for K and A′[T] is finite.

accepted.question_text: Let K/Q be a Galois extension containing the p-th roots of unity, let H be the maximal unramified p-abelian extension of the cyclotomic Zp-extension K∞, and let HE′ be the subextension cut out by adjoining p-power roots of global units. Must the index [H : HE′] always be finite? This is the general Greenberg conjecture in the paper's formulation, and it asks whether the unramified Iwasawa module is always controlled up to finite index by the unit-generated extension.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. Let K/Q be an arbitrary galois extension containing the p-th roots of unity and H/K∞ the maximal unramified p - abelian extension of its cyclotomic Zp-extension. Let HE′ = H ∩ ΩE, with ΩE = ∪nKn[E1/pn n ] and En = O(Kn). Then [H : HE′] < ∞.
"It would be an important problem, to find out when dim(V+) > 0";

accepted.question_text: For a CM Galois extension K containing the p-th roots of unity, is the minus-part T-torsion in the p-unit class-group module trivial; that is, does (A′)^−[T] = {1} hold? This is the classical Gross conjecture in the paper's formulation, expressing that the minus-part p-unit class module has no nontrivial T-torsion.

evidence.quote: This is a conjecture of Gross [3], which follows from the elementary lemma below and the decomposition A−[T] = (A′)−[T] ⊕ B−.

trace.notes: Mapped the two-part PDF and isolated explicit problem regions in the SNOQIT I introduction, SNOQIT II §§3.4-4, and Appendices B and D.
Expanded the brief Property F question into a standalone formulation that includes both example-finding and structural criteria for free Λ-submodules.
Normalized the generalized Gross-Kuz'min conjecture to the finiteness of A′[T] and preserved the paper's CM-only partial resolution as evidence context.
Rewrote the unit-rank defect discussion as the general Leopoldt conjecture, using the paper's own statement that the full conjecture remains open in general.

Merged the explicit Greenberg conjecture with Iwasawa's equivalent motivating question about when dim(V+) is positive, since both point to the same unit-vs-unramified obstruction phenomenon in this source.
Marked the Gross conjecture item as solved because the same source both states the conjectural form and later proves Theorem 5 establishing (A′)−[T] = {1}.
